newsitem.title: USA: CBOT March wheat up on weather/cash, others drop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT March wheat up on weather/cash, others drop.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mixed with nearby March higher on weather-related transportation tie-ups in the U.S. Great Plains and Dakotas, traders said.
"The transportation slowdown is potentially a problem, it's going to tighten up the stocks," said Skip Searcy, wheat trading specialist for FIMAT Futures.
Traders said the bitter cold temperatures and snow in the U.S. was slowing movement of wheat and boosting nearby cash basis markets.
Gains were limited by slow exports.
News Algeria overnight bought another 50,000 tonnes of wheat from France rather than the U.S. weighed on the market, traders said.

New-crop July was lower on diminished concerns about weather-damage to the U.S. winter wheat crop. Wheat surged Friday on a bullish USDA seedings report and cold temperatures in the U.S. winter wheat growing region also boosted prices.
But snowfall in key U.S. winter wheat growing areas tempered worries that cold weather could damage the crop.
Wheat closed 2-1/4 cents per bushel higher to three lower, with March, the only gainer, up 2-1/4 at $3.90-1/4.
SAK Futures bought two million bushels of March and E.D. and F. Man International bought 1.5 million bushels of March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 11,000 contracts, below the 13,339 traded Tuesday, according to the CBOT.

In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 300 July $3.10 puts at 3-1/2 cents, E.D. and F. Man International bought 300 July $3.60 puts at 22 cents and Continental Grain bought 100 March $3.50 puts at 1/2 cent, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 5,000 contracts, about the same as 5,086 traded Tuesday.
